intelligence.human_view: His eye and the captain's eye found the same fault independently, minutes apart. The captain's-eye walk of the staged Hub (browser task 9a549b46, 19:41–19:51Z) pixel-sampled the right sidebar: My Worlds ~#a21caf deep magenta, Favorite Worlds ~#8e24aa purple-magenta — adjacent purples — and the same fault again at the bottom of the list (White Paper ~#a21caf, Pricing ~#8e24aa) and in the left sidebar (Hub magenta / Dashboard purple; Smart Factory magenta / Smart Growth purple). The hex values differ between the purple neighbors, but the eye reads them as the same color twice in a row, which breaks the feed's own rule in SN-3062, "Spectrum flow (never the same color twice in a row)." The same fault sits in the Leaderboards boards — Overall and Top area both read purple/magenta (eye flagged it 19:41–19:46Z, fix round dispatched 19:46Z) — so this is not one list's problem. The spectrum flow is judged by the eye, not by the hex table: two hexes that differ on paper and read as one color on the screen are the same color, as far as the person looking is concerned — and the person looking is the only judge that counts.
intelligence.simple_view: You know the colors on the sides, like a rainbow? The top one and the one under it look the same — both purple! You have to make them different enough that you can tell them apart just by looking. If you can't tell, the colors are wrong!
intelligence.grandma_view: You know the colors on the sides, love, like a rainbow? The top one and the one under it look the same — both purple, dear! You have to make them different enough that you can tell them apart just by looking. If you can't tell, the colors are wrong!
